draft.title: Alpha, beta and gamma radiation
card: Some nuclei are unstable. They decay by giving off radiation until they become stable.
Alpha
a particle of two protons and two neutrons. It travels only a few centimetres in air and is stopped by paper.
Beta
a fast electron from the nucleus. It travels about a metre in air and is stopped by a thin sheet of aluminium.
Gamma
a ray of energy, not a particle. It goes very far and is only reduced by thick lead or concrete.
draft.remember: Alpha is stopped most easily, beta less so, and gamma goes the furthest.

a.q: Which type of radiation is stopped by a sheet of paper?
a.why: Alpha particles are large and are stopped by paper. Beta particles pass through paper and need aluminium, and gamma rays go through both.
a.clue: Which radiation travels the shortest distance?

b.q: A worker needs a barrier that blocks beta particles but is not thick lead. Which barrier suits best?
b.why: Aluminium stops beta particles. Paper does not, because beta passes through it. Beta particles travel about a metre in air, so a few centimetres of air does not stop them.
b.clue: Beta passes through paper but not metal sheet.

problems.detail: The clue 'Beta passes through paper but not metal sheet' gives the answer away. Aluminium is the only metal option, so a student can pick it without knowing the idea.

'It goes very far and is only reduced by thick lead or concrete' suggests other materials do not reduce gamma at all. In fact every material reduces gamma somewhat; thick lead or concrete just reduces it greatly. Better: 'is greatly reduced by thick lead or concrete'.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer. Question b's clue names metal as the barrier, which gives the answer away, and the card's 'only reduced by thick lead or concrete' wrongly suggests other materials do not reduce gamma at all.

proposal.title: Alpha, beta and gamma radiation
card: Some nuclei are unstable. They decay by giving off radiation until they become stable.
Alpha
a particle of two protons and two neutrons. It travels only a few centimetres in air and is stopped by paper.
Beta
a fast electron from the nucleus. It travels about a metre in air and is stopped by a thin sheet of aluminium.
Gamma
a ray of energy, not a particle. It travels a long way through air and most materials, and is greatly reduced by thick lead or concrete.
proposal.remember: Alpha is stopped most easily, beta less so, and gamma goes the furthest.

a.q: Which type of radiation is stopped by a sheet of paper?
a.why: Alpha particles are large and are stopped by paper. Beta particles pass through paper and need aluminium to stop them, and gamma rays go through both.
a.clue: Which radiation travels the shortest distance?

b.q: A detector is near a radioactive source. A sheet of paper between them does not change the reading, but a thin sheet of aluminium cuts it to almost zero. What is the source giving off?
b.why: The radiation gets through paper, so it is not alpha. It is stopped by thin aluminium, so it is not gamma, which would pass through and keep the reading up. Only beta fits both results.
b.clue: Use each barrier to rule out one type.
